page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance from the Cloud GPU family. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance includes two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs with a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific workloads, particularly in LLM inference. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches a top-tier 8,665.1 tokens per second, while text generation averages 260.3 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing achieves a top-tier 613.27 tokens per second, and text generation reaches a strong 32.35 tokens per second. General CPU benchmarks show average performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,449.0 and a multi-core score of 9,569.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 102.38 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 53.61 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated Intel CPU cores with dual NVIDIA Ampere GPUs and a substantial 128 GB memory footprint. This hardware profile is well-suited for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations. The inclusion of local NVMe storage also supports data-intensive applications that require fast local read/write capabilities alongside GPU acceleration.
description: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It features 12 dedicated Intel vCPUs (6 physical cores) running at 2.0 GHz, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a 700 GB NVMe SSD. The instance is equipped with two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a total of 32 GB of VRAM. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM prompt processing, reaching 8,665.1 tokens per second for a 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second for a 7B model. General CPU and memory benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,569.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 20,085.48, fall within the average range. This configuration is highly suitable for small-to-medium language model inference, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations requiring local NVMe storage.
